p01.why: A function declared at block scope inside a function template is not a templated entity and cannot have a trailing clause.

p02.why: T::type is not valid for int, so the compound requirement fails and the concept is false.

p03.why: The body of a requires expression must have at least one requirement.

p04.why: The trailing requires clause comes before the trailing return type.

p05.why: Both clause positions constrain the call operator, and an attribute after the first clause appertains to the lambda.

p06.why: A call in a requires clause needs parentheses.

p07.why: Concepts can have constant, template template, and pack parameters, and any logical_or_expr.

p08.why: A requires expression is a bool constant inside or outside a template, and these requirements are valid.

p09.why: typename T::tag fails first, so Trap<int> is not substituted.

p10.why: The attribute appertains to the concept; the use gives at most a warning. Clang 18 rejects the attribute (Q-0270).

p11.why: A concept's head must not have a constrained template parameter.

p12.why: A template template parameter can have a requires clause, and Box has the same constraint.

p13.why: The concept-id is checked inside a member of Box, where secret is accessible, so it is true.

p14.why: noexcept(f()) is true for quiet's pointer and false for loud's.

p15.why: Step 2 fails because grow is not noexcept, so the extra argument is not substituted. Clang substitutes it first and rejects (Q-0287).

p16.why: A friend declaration must not declare a concept.

p17.why: A concept must not be specialized.

p18.why: A type after -> is not valid; it must be a type constraint.

p19.why: A lambda in a default member initializer of a class template can have a trailing clause; EDG rejects (Q-0260).

p20.why: A nested concept-id or a dependent requirement gives false without an error.

p21.why: Each compound requirement checks decltype((E)), so int&, int&&, int, T&, and double hold for Thing; char is not Big.

p22.why: A negation in a requires clause needs parentheses.

p23.why: A function with no return deduces void, and Wide<void> is not satisfied.

p24.why: A requires-expression parameter must not have the name of an enclosing template parameter.

p25.why: The requirements hold for Counter; assigning through const is not valid, so Assigns is false.

p26.why: A concept's head must not have a requires clause.

p27.why: The requirement is checked inside a member of Box, where secret is accessible, so it is true; GCC 14 gives false (Q-0288).

p28.why: At namespace scope secret is not accessible, so the concept is false.

p29.why: The parameter has the name of the template parameter T.

p30.why: A concept must not use its own name.

p31.why: The requirements are not evaluated, so counter stays 0 and never needs no definition.

p32.why: A concept must not be partially specialized.

p33.why: A virtual function must not have a trailing requires clause; GCC accepts (Q-0258).

p34.why: A constrained placeholder must not appear in a structured binding; EDG accepts (Q-0286).

p35.why: Wide<char> fails, so pick<'a'> has a deduction failure and no other candidate.

p36.why: A concept name before a declarator needs auto.

p37.why: The nested requirement uses the parameter t outside an unevaluated operand. Clang 18 gives false (Q-0289).

p38.why: The trailing clause comes before the trailing return type.

p39.why: A call that selects a deleted function is not valid, so Twiceable<double> is false.

p40.why: Outside a template the requirement selects a deleted function, which makes the program not valid.

p41.why: The return type deduces char, and Big<char> is false.

p42.why: A comparison in a requires clause needs parentheses.

p43.why: Returning a void expression deduces void, and Wide<void> is not satisfied.

p44.why: The parameter list must not end with an ellipsis; GCC accepts (Q-0259).

p45.why: When the concept's first parameter is a pack, each check gives it one element, so One holds for each.

p46.why: Stack<int, 0> fails its constraint, and the requirement depends on no template parameter.

p47.why: A trailing clause must not follow the declarator of a pointer to function.

p48.why: The trailing clause follows the trailing return type, and both clauses hold for int.

p49.why: The requirement is true for Box and false for int, so 4 + 1 == 5.

p50.why: A function that is not templated cannot have a trailing clause.

p51.why: A comparison in a requires clause needs parentheses.

p52.why: A parameter must not have a default argument; GCC accepts (Q-0259).

p53.why: T::missing fails, so Trap<int> is not checked.

p54.why: Positive's first parameter is a constant parameter, so Positive is not a type concept.

p55.why: The requirement depends on no template parameter and is not valid, also in a template never instantiated.

p56.why: A constrained placeholder must not appear in a functional cast.

p57.why: Parameter types adjust as in a function, to T* and T(*)(int).

p58.why: A trailing clause must not follow the type in a new expression.

p59.why: A concept must not use its own name.

p60.why: Requires expressions in a variable template and if constexpr give true for Tagged and false for int.

p61.why: Each kind of template can have a requires clause; Kind<char*> uses the primary.

p62.why: (void) means no parameters, and 1 is valid.

p63.why: decltype(auto) must not be the type of a function parameter.

p64.why: A generic lambda can have a trailing clause, and sizeof(int) > 1.

p65.why: Derived<int>::get overrides a virtual function, so it is virtual and must not have a trailing clause; GCC accepts (Q-0258).

p66.why: A concept-id is a bool constant in an array bound, case labels, noexcept, and a conditional.

p67.why: A concept-id is a prvalue bool constant.

p68.why: The constraint applies to the invented parameter, and an explicit argument gives it double.

p69.why: The first check inside the member is true; the later check at namespace scope changes the result, which needs no diagnostic, and every compiler keeps the first result.

p70.why: Wide<char> fails for the constant argument.

p71.why: Two arguments for a one-parameter concept are not valid.

p72.why: A concept must not be defined in a block.

p73.why: A trailing clause must not follow the declarator of a parameter.

p74.why: A lambda inside a function template is templated and can have a trailing clause; EDG rejects (Q-0260).

p75.why: A concept's one declaration is its definition.

p76.why: Members of a class template and of a class inside one can have a trailing clause.

p77.why: A specialization that fails its constraints or default arguments is not valid, so the concepts are false.

p78.why: A member of a local class inside a function template can have a trailing clause; EDG rejects (Q-0260).

p79.why: A parameter must not have a placeholder type.

p80.why: A qualified concept name works as a type constraint.

p81.why: Narrowing in braces is not valid, so double and long long give false.

p82.why: A type requirement does not instantiate the class, so incomplete Never and Broken are fine.

p83.why: Member types, member templates, and specializations can be named; int& * is not valid.

p84.why: The constraint checks the deduced type alone: int, int, int, int&, int&.

p85.why: The attribute appertains to an unused concept. Clang 18 rejects the attribute (Q-0270).

p86.why: Each pack constraint is one atomic fold, so neither template subsumes the other and the call is ambiguous; EDG orders them (Q-0285).

p87.why: (void) means no parameters, so Makes<int> is true; Clang gives false inside a template (Q-0290).

p88.why: An empty pack satisfies the constraint, and char fails it.

p89.why: noexcept appears only in a compound requirement.

p90.why: No object is made, so the type need not be constructible; a later parameter can use an earlier one.

p91.why: A type requirement must not name a keyword type.

p92.why: A requires clause can hold a requires expression, so requires appears twice.

p93.why: The constrained template fails for 'a', so the other one is chosen.

p94.why: A member of a class that is not templated cannot have a trailing clause.

p95.why: The expression is valid, though false.

p96.why: Both clauses must hold: int passes, char and Huge fail.

p97.why: A concept must not be defined in a class.

p98.why: ADL finds lib::use; the global use is declared after the template and ADL for other::B finds nothing, so both forms give false for B.

p99.why: A constrained placeholder must not appear in a functional cast.

p100.why: Pair<T> lacks an argument for U, so the type constraint gives an invalid list.

p101.why: t.missing() fails at step 1, so Trap is not substituted. Clang substitutes the extra argument first and rejects (Q-0287).

p102.why: int().size() depends on no template parameter and is not valid.

p103.why: A concept must not be explicitly instantiated.

p104.why: Wide<int> holds for 3; Value<'a'> fails its constraint, so Takes<'a'> is false.

p105.why: A virtual function must not have a trailing clause; GCC accepts (Q-0258).

p106.why: Each operand is a primary expression, and the clause holds.

p107.why: The expressions are valid and not evaluated.

p108.why: A constant for a type parameter does not match in kind.

p109.why: SameAs<int> before T gives SameAs<T, int>.

p110.why: A friend defined in a class template can have a trailing clause.

p111.why: sizeof(t) is unevaluated; the conjunction stops at the false part; requires false gives false.

p112.why: T::type is not valid for int, so the requirement fails and the concept is false.

p113.why: The parameter is used only in sizeof.

p114.why: The first check at namespace scope gives false, the member's later check would differ, which needs no diagnostic, and every compiler keeps the first result.

p115.why: The default is checked only when a template-id uses it, and int satisfies Wide.

p116.why: A trailing clause must not follow the declarator of a variable.

p117.why: Positive is not a type concept.

p118.why: The constrained guide is skipped for char and wins for int.

p119.why: Concepts with auto, packs of constants, and calls in the expression work.

p120.why: A concept must not be declared again.

p121.why: The constraint before auto... applies to each element; char fails.

p122.why: decltype(auto) on the name n deduces int, and LvalueRef<int> is false.

p123.why: Box<> uses the default char, which fails Wide.

p124.why: Outside a template, an invalid requirement makes the program not valid.
